title: Block: Count With a Hashmap
oneLiner: Count every character with a hashmap, then return the most common one, ties going to the one that appears first.
keyTakeaway: Counting is the hashmap construct you write most: read the old count with a default of 0, add one, store it back. Get the missing-key case right once and it stops being a bug.
explanation:
Return the character that appears most often in s. When several share the highest count, return the one whose first appearance is earliest. An empty string returns an empty string.

Two passes. The first builds the counts: counts.GetValueOrDefault(c) + 1 in C#, counts.get(c, 0) + 1 in Python. The second walks s again in order and keeps the first character whose count beats the best so far. Replacing only on a strictly higher count is what sends ties to the earliest character.

This is a rep, not a puzzle: write it from the blank editor until the counting line comes out without thinking.

gotchas: Reading counts[c] before the key exists: use GetValueOrDefault, get(c, 0) or a defaultdict.
Replacing the best on an equal count, which sends ties to the last character instead of the first.

complexity.note: Two passes over the n characters with O(1) average map work each. The map holds one entry per distinct character: O(n) in general, O(1) if you count the alphabet as fixed.
